title: Aldana Whitcombe Family Law — a before/after website makeover
description: A before/after makeover for an invented Dallas family-law office. The old site is a 940 px table with pale 11 px Times, a gold phone-number image, practice areas as a picture, a 6.2 MB skyline (simulated), "GUARANTEED RESULTS!!!", and Attorney JSON-LD that isn't valid JSON because of a trailing comma. The calm rebuild has one clear action (request a consultation), tap-to-call, live office hours in US Central time, plain practice-area copy, a careful intake form, an attorney-advertising disclaimer and LegalService JSON-LD. It's all marked as fictional, with a 'What changed' panel and 11 in-page checks (not Lighthouse) scoring both versions.
prompt: Make a before/after website makeover for a fictional Dallas family-law office as proof for my $1,200 Landing Page, Built + Tested package. Be careful with the legal copy: no guarantees of outcomes, and a generic attorney-advertising style disclaimer that's clearly marked fictional. The before should be a believable dated site with tiny low-contrast text, no clear call to action, the phone number and practice areas as images, a slow huge hero (simulated), no hours, no meta description and no mobile layout, in a scaled frame so the page doesn't scroll sideways. The after should be mobile-first and accessible, with tap-to-call, office hours with open/closed-now in Central time, a map-free location block, a consultation CTA, sample reviews that are labelled as samples, an FAQ and LegalService JSON-LD. Include a keyboard-accessible toggle, a 'What changed' panel linked to highlighted areas, a live in-page scorecard that is clearly not Lighthouse, a CTA to my services section and a footer saying it's fictional.

methodology: Independent oracle for the scorecard: raw computed styles, rects and head tags come out of each frame, and all 11 checks are judged in Node with the spec's own WCAG luminance code. The spec then compares each check's pass flag and counts with the page's data attributes for both versions, and again after switching preview widths and after the intake form adds a status line.

The broken structured data is tested for real: the old site's JSON-LD contains "@type": "Attorney", JSON.parse in Node must throw a SyntaxError on it, and the scorecard must report it as 'invalid'. The new LegalService JSON-LD must parse, match the tel: links, and match the hours table day by day.

Legal copy as assertions: the footer disclaimer must say attorney advertising, not legal advice, no attorney–client relationship and no promised outcome, and it must say the firm is fictional. Outside that disclaimer, the new site's text must not match guarantee, win or aggressive. The intake form cannot be sent until the no-relationship acknowledgement is ticked.

Office hours under page.clock: the 5:30 PM close on a Thursday in daylight time is checked in two browser contexts set to Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles. The 8:30 AM Monday opening, the 4 PM Friday close, Saturday ('opens Monday') and Sunday ('opens tomorrow') are checked in standard time, against the test's own hours table and the published US DST offsets.

Behaviour: the tab toggle driven with Arrow, Home, End and Tab keys; each 'What changed' button highlights exactly one element in the right frame and scrolls it into view; no page overflow at 360 px with the old 980 px layout shown; and no network requests from the demo form.
risks: The disclaimer is generic, and the page says so. Real lawyer advertising is governed by state bar rules, including rules on testimonials, so a real firm would need its own review.
Contrast is judged against background-color only; text over images or gradients would be misjudged, so the rebuild keeps text on solid fills.

The spec and the page choose text elements by the same definition, so a shared blind spot is possible. A deliberate change to one threshold was caught; a change in a range no element falls into was not.

Schema.org describes LegalService as more inclusive than the older Attorney type, so the page uses LegalService. The check accepts either type, so switching back to Attorney would not fail the scorecard.
qa.playwright: Most of the spec is shared with the other two makeovers. The Node-side oracle, frameLocator for reading the srcdoc frames, and page.clock with pauseAt and runFor(61 s) at each boundary work the same way here. What's specific to this page is asserting a JSON.parse failure in Node for the broken JSON-LD, and using a clone of the frame's body with the disclaimer removed, so the 'no guarantees' regex can't pass or fail just because of the disclaimer's own wording. Native form validation turned out to be easy to test: clicking submit without the required checkbox leaves the status line empty, because no submit event fires. browser.newContext({ timezoneId }) checks the same instant under two machine time zones. There is no visual snapshot, so styling regressions in the mock sites would go unnoticed.
coverage: Scorecard vs independent oracle, both versions, both preview widths
WCAG AA contrast of the whole rebuild, formula reference values
LegalService JSON-LD vs visible phone and hours; the old JSON-LD fails JSON.parse
Office hours across CDT and CST boundaries, the early Friday close, the weekend
Disclaimer wording, no promised outcomes, required acknowledgement on the intake form
Tap-to-call, keyboard tabs, no horizontal scroll at 360 px, 'What changed' highlights, services CTA

a11y: The toggle is a WAI-ARIA tablist with a roving tabindex and Arrow, Home and End keys. The hidden frame is inert. Frames have descriptive titles, fix buttons name the fix they show, and changes are announced through aria-live. The scorecard is a table with headers. In the rebuild, every field has a visible label, the acknowledgement checkbox is 24 px and wrapped in its label, the map has a text alternative, and all text passes WCAG AA by the page's own check.
